cases.prompt: install my mac apps - chrome, slack, spotify, the usual
which gui apps should a developer install on a new mac
install raycast and a window manager
set up a terminal app - warp, ghostty or iterm2?
install amphetamine to keep my mac awake
get me a database gui like dbeaver or tableplus
install zoom, figma and a vpn client
install apps from the app store via the command line
kit out this new macbook with the standard productivity apps
install ripgrep, fzf and the cli tools
install and configure vs code
install docker desktop or orbstack
install homebrew
set up my whole mac from scratch
configure raycast hotkeys and extensions in depth
install the aws cli and kubectl
install claude code and the ai coding clis
Install the standard app set on my new Mac: browser, comms, terminal, launcher, utilities.
expected_behavior: asks which groups/apps the user wants instead of installing a fixed list; installs via brew casks with correct current tokens
handles App Store-only apps (e.g. Amphetamine) via mas with the id, telling the user to sign into the App Store app first since mas cannot sign in
flags apps needing manual steps after install: launcher hotkey remap for Raycast, license keys, VPN sign-ins
notes GUI apps mostly self-update (auto_updates casks) so plain brew upgrade skips them
does not install CLI-only tools, editors, or container runtimes

cases.prompt: i need a terminal app recommendation and install
expected_behavior: offers the 2026 trio with one-line tradeoffs - Ghostty (recommended default: fast, native, open source), Warp (AI features, optional account), iTerm2 (mature, most configurable) - and installs the chosen one
reminds about selecting the Nerd Font in the new terminal's profile if a prompt theme is in use
does not switch the user's shell or prompt config

cases.prompt: install messenger and filezilla like my old setup guide says
expected_behavior: flags that the messenger cask is deprecated/disabled and filezilla has no cask - offers current alternatives (web messenger.com, or direct download; Cyberduck/Transmit for file transfer) instead of failing silently
